free_text: The 66-year-old male presents with a high PSA of 12.0 and a biopsy-confirmed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP Grade Group 3) adenocarcinoma localized to the mid-left peripheral zone, with a PI-RADS score of 3 on MRI. He has mild LUTS and chronic kidney disease. The management assessment indicates that individual treatment benefit and patient preferences require clinical review, representing the trade-off between local control and potential side effects of definitive treatment.
